A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoLA and provide readable methods, results, equations, figures, and appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval and commonsense evaluations, scoring ablations, memory-collision visualizations, and kernel simulations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds harder-RULER comparisons, cache-parameter experiments, and timing and VRAM measurements.

M1.justification: V2's SRE is v1's self-recall score. The three memory systems, cache-selection and update procedures, distillation, chunkwise inference, and decoding pseudocode are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca, the same commonsense benchmarks, and the full RULER task set. The harder RULER tasks already appear in v1 Appendix F; v2's additional parameter and efficiency experiments reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: The harder-RULER evaluation expands from LoLA alone in v1 Table 7 to comparisons with enlarged-window LoLCATs-8B+ and Mamba2-8B in v2 Table 2. Table 4 additionally evaluates an attention-score caching heuristic inspired by H2O and LESS.

E3.justification: The harder-RULER evaluation changes from mixed 2K/4K contexts to uniform 4K contexts. V1 specifies C=λ=512; v2 reports η=128, λ=768 for LoLA and η=896 for LoLCATs. New Appendix B introduces cache-size sweeps measuring latency, peak VRAM, and variable-tracking accuracy.

E4.justification: New Appendix B systematically analyzes cache allocation, speed, memory consumption, and variable-tracking performance. Table 4 adds an attention-score selection ablation. The earlier scoring alternatives, kernel simulations, and memory-collision analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 4 reports timing averaged over 100 trials, adding repeated-measurement information absent from v1. No increased run count for retained accuracy experiments, confidence intervals, or significance tests is reported.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the harder-RULER results under revised settings, reporting average accuracies of 45.2% for LoLA, 6.7% for LoLCATs, and 39.7% for Mamba2. It adds efficiency results and a 10.6% attention-score ablation result. Commonsense scores remain unchanged. V2 Table 1 reports 99.9% for largest-cache S-NIAH-1 at 4K, conflicting with the retained 99.0% in its Tables 7–8 and v1.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix F, Equation 21, adds a mathematical definition of the newly evaluated caching score by accumulating exponential query-key similarities across the window. The kernel/SVD bound and core self-recall mathematics remain unchanged; the new interpolation notation restates the existing perfect-recall condition.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly elevates the necessity of the self-recall metric into an abstract and introduction contribution, whereas v1 emphasizes the necessity of sparse caching. It removes consumer-GPU reproducibility as a headline contribution. The central inference-only method and retrieval and commonsense claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation that similar haystack phrases can mislead query-dependent cache selection, motivating LoLA's query-agnostic score. Appendix B develops practical speed, memory, and accuracy tradeoff guidance. The underlying memory-collision interpretation and need for larger caches on difficult tasks are retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents explicit cache parameters, RTX 4090 efficiency measurements, VRAM accounting, and exclusion of data-loading time from latency. Its new reproducibility statement identifies available LoLCATs 8B base weights and promises full code for the camera-ready version. The training recipe and pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Liger, Lizard, H2O, LESS, Atlas, and LaCT, and removes the Bietti memory-viewpoint citation. It expands positioning against attention-based cache selection and updates future architectural directions, while retaining the central relationship to LoLCATs and hybrid attention.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and substantial introductory, preliminary, method, and retrieval discussion. It standardizes SRE terminology, adds a reproducibility statement, and reorganizes the appendices, including moving detailed single-needle discussion out of the main text.

P2.justification: V2 adds four efficiency/cache figures, redesigns main Table 1 around explicit cache parameters, and retains its fuller predecessor in Appendix C. The harder-RULER comparison replaces the main extended-retrieval display, whose results move to the appendix. Typography, headings, and page layout change throughout; existing scientific plots are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens practical validation: harder RULER tasks gain a matching-cache LoLCATs control and a Mamba2 comparison, while Appendix B supplies measured latency, VRAM, and accuracy tradeoffs missing from v1. These address important empirical gaps. Revised settings prevent interpreting the new scores as same-setting gains over v1, and the 99.9% versus 99.0% table conflict is a limited reporting regression that does not outweigh the stronger validation.
